evidence.quote: The tensile studies revealed that the fractures occurred within the weld zone due to high welding residual stresses and metallurgical change caused by welding heat input.
The plates are extracted using EDM process in 150 × 120 × 10 mm were used for HLAW with wire feed rate (WFR) of 10 m/min, and 300 × 120 × 10 mm plates were utilized for HLAW with a WFR of 11 m/min.

Figure 2a and b show the HLAW process, which included a Y -shaped edge with a 20° angle and a 1.5 mm root face, with a 0.2 mm root gap for a WFR of 10 m/min and while no gap is employed at a WFR of 11 m/min.
From Eqs. (1)&( 2), the total heat input for the 10 m/min and 11 m/min wire feed rate welded joints are 0.516 kJ/mm and 0.615 kJ/mm, respectively.

machine_learning_models.name: linear regression (LR)
machine_learning_models.task: prediction of room and high temperature tensile strength of HLAW Inconel 617 joints
machine_learning_models.dataset: 12 experimental tensile tests on HLAW joints

evidence.quote: This works deals with the application of various regression analysis methods like Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree Regression (DTR), Random Forest Regression (RFR), Polynomial Regression (PR), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) and Support V ector Regression (SVR) were used for predicting the room and high temperature tensile behaviour of hybrid laser arc welded Inconel 617 alloy.
